import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def mergeSort_precond (v : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Merge two lists, taking the smaller head at each step. -/
def mergeTwo : List Int → List Int → List Int
  | [], ys => ys
  | xs, [] => xs
  | x :: xs, y :: ys =>
      if x ≤ y then x :: mergeTwo xs (y :: ys) else y :: mergeTwo (x :: xs) ys
termination_by xs ys => xs.length + ys.length

/-- Recursive divide-and-conquer merge sort: split in half, sort halves, merge. -/
def msort (l : List Int) : List Int :=
  if h : l.length ≤ 1 then l
  else mergeTwo (msort (l.take (l.length / 2))) (msort (l.drop (l.length / 2)))
termination_by l.length
decreasing_by
  · simp only [List.length_take]; omega
  · simp only [List.length_drop]; omega
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def mergeSort (v : List Int) (h_precond : mergeSort_precond v) : List Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  msort v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def mergeSort_postcond (v : List Int) (result : List Int) (h_precond : mergeSort_precond v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
   List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) result ∧ result.Perm v
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem mergeTwo_perm : ∀ (xs ys : List Int), (mergeTwo xs ys).Perm (xs ++ ys)
  | [], ys => by simp [mergeTwo]
  | x :: xs, [] => by simp [mergeTwo]
  | x :: xs, y :: ys => by
      rw [mergeTwo]
      split
      · exact (mergeTwo_perm xs (y :: ys)).cons x
      · exact ((mergeTwo_perm (x :: xs) ys).cons y).trans List.perm_middle.symm
termination_by xs ys => xs.length + ys.length

theorem mergeTwo_sorted : ∀ (xs ys : List Int), List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) xs →
    List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) ys → List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (mergeTwo xs ys)
  | [], ys, _, hy => by simpa [mergeTwo] using hy
  | x :: xs, [], hx, _ => by simpa [mergeTwo] using hx
  | x :: xs, y :: ys, hx, hy => by
      rw [mergeTwo]
      split
      · rename_i hxy
        refine List.sorted_cons.2 ⟨?_, mergeTwo_sorted xs (y :: ys) hx.of_cons hy⟩
        intro b hb
        rcases List.mem_append.1 ((mergeTwo_perm xs (y :: ys)).subset hb) with h | h
        · exact List.rel_of_sorted_cons hx b h
        · rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
          · exact hxy
          · exact le_trans hxy (List.rel_of_sorted_cons hy b h)
      · rename_i hxy
        have hyx : y ≤ x := le_of_lt (lt_of_not_le hxy)
        refine List.sorted_cons.2 ⟨?_, mergeTwo_sorted (x :: xs) ys hx hy.of_cons⟩
        intro b hb
        rcases List.mem_append.1 ((mergeTwo_perm (x :: xs) ys).subset hb) with h | h
        · rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
          · exact hyx
          · exact le_trans hyx (List.rel_of_sorted_cons hx b h)
        · exact List.rel_of_sorted_cons hy b h
termination_by xs ys => xs.length + ys.length

theorem msort_perm (l : List Int) : (msort l).Perm l := by
  rw [msort]
  split
  · exact List.Perm.refl l
  · rename_i h
    have h1 := mergeTwo_perm (msort (l.take (l.length / 2))) (msort (l.drop (l.length / 2)))
    have h2 : (msort (l.take (l.length / 2)) ++ msort (l.drop (l.length / 2))).Perm
        (l.take (l.length / 2) ++ l.drop (l.length / 2)) :=
      (msort_perm _).append (msort_perm _)
    have h3 := h1.trans h2
    rwa [List.take_append_drop] at h3
termination_by l.length
decreasing_by
  · simp only [List.length_take]; omega
  · simp only [List.length_drop]; omega

theorem msort_sorted (l : List Int) : List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (msort l) := by
  rw [msort]
  split
  · rename_i h
    match l, h with
    | [], _ => exact List.sorted_nil
    | [a], _ => exact List.sorted_singleton a
    | a :: b :: t, h => simp at h
  · exact mergeTwo_sorted _ _ (msort_sorted _) (msort_sorted _)
termination_by l.length
decreasing_by
  · simp only [List.length_take]; omega
  · simp only [List.length_drop]; omega
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem mergeSort_postcond_satisfied (v : List Int) (h_precond : mergeSort_precond v) :
    mergeSort_postcond v (mergeSort v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  exact ⟨msort_sorted v, msort_perm v⟩
  -- !benchmark @end proof

`./check.sh` prints **LEAN VERIFIED** (only warnings: unused teacher-provided variables and one deprecation of `lt_of_not_le`).

## What I implemented

In `auxcode` (`Solution.lean:11-27`):
- `mergeTwo` — genuine merge of two lists, taking the smaller head each step, terminating on `xs.length + ys.length`.
- `msort` — recursive divide-and-conquer: base case `length ≤ 1` returns the list, otherwise `mergeTwo (msort (take (n/2))) (msort (drop (n/2)))`, terminating on `l.length` with explicit `decreasing_by` proofs.

In `code`: `mergeSort v _ := msort v`.

In `lemma`: four real lemmas — `mergeTwo_perm` (`mergeTwo xs ys ~ xs ++ ys`), `mergeTwo_sorted` (merge of two sorted lists is sorted, via membership through the permutation), and `msort_perm` / `msort_sorted` by well-founded recursion mirroring the algorithm.

In `proof`: `⟨msort_sorted v, msort_perm v⟩`.

## Semantic audit against TASK.md

- **Algorithm**: recursive split/sort/merge as specified — not a library sort, not an oracle, no `Nat.find`, `Classical.choose`, `decide`, or brute force. `List.mergeSort` is never used.
- **Postcondition (1) sorted**: proved from a real merge-preserves-sortedness lemma, not a placeholder.
- **Postcondition (2) permutation**: proved via `mergeTwo_perm` + `List.take_append_drop`, so multiplicities (duplicates) are preserved — not a weaker "same elements" claim.
- **Preconditions**: none required; the teacher's `True` precond and the postcond block are untouched.
- **Recursion**: `partial` avoided in favor of termination proofs, as the task's note permits. Splitting at `n/2` when `length ≥ 2` gives both halves strictly shorter — that's exactly what the `decreasing_by` goals discharge, so there's no unfounded recursion.
- **Edge cases**: `[]` and `[a]` hit the `length ≤ 1` branch and are returned as-is (both sorted and trivially permutations). All-negative and mixed-sign inputs are handled: comparisons use `Int`'s `≤` with no positivity assumption anywhere. Equal elements go to the `x ≤ y` branch, so nothing is dropped.
- **Markers**: all four editable marker pairs plus the precond/postcond markers are present and unchanged; no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `unsafe`, `extern`, or `implemented_by` in any editable section.

One cosmetic item left as-is: `lt_of_not_le` in `mergeTwo_sorted` is deprecated in favor of `lt_of_not_ge`. It compiles and only emits a warning.
